finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the boolean result instead of calling require_edit(), so the authorization check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can overwrite the body of any document they do not own or edit.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with a JSON body {"body": ...} for a doc_id they have no edit rights on.
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] (docs.py:20), the write to the document body.

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> accepts attacker-controlled doc_id and JSON body
doc = DOCS[doc_id] fetches the target doc with no ownership check
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns False for a non-editor, but the return value is ignored and abort(403) is never reached

finding.guards_checked: Compared with update_title (docs.py:27), which correctly uses require_edit and aborts with 403. No decorator, before_request hook, or other check protects update_doc in this file. g.user is assumed to be set by an authentication mechanism that is not present in this directory. Even if it is set, there is no authorization on this route.

verdict.reason: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(), which only returns a bool (docs.py:7-8), and discards the result, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] without any abort; only require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts, and it is used only in update_title (docs.py:27).
